title: The Safe route over the hill
subtitle: 安全预防 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 安全预防（人与自然·灾害防范·安全与预防）
meta: 主题语境：安全预防（人与自然·灾害防范·安全与预防）　|　核心词汇：safe　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 safe 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1989 the fisherman wrote of ① a safe route over the hill in the logbook, and everybody in the harbour said at once that it was ② safer than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the fisherman, who never explained anything, had done it in public and gone home; it was the safe ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the safest route over the hill anybody in the harbour had ever seen, or so the logbook for July 1983 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too safe to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the boatman who had come to help; the safe ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the net at the far pier, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a safe place for the money, and said that no boatman in his right mind would call it ⑥ as safe as the place for the money they had once had in the old harbour. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was safe or not, and he said so.

By 1996 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the logbook. What the line asked for was ⑦ something safe, and nothing besides. The boatman from the next harbour called the whole plan ⑧ quite safe; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the logbook kept the names of the safe ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1999, in silence, she wrote of another safe route over the hill in the same logbook, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ safer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The safest place for the money in the whole harbour, she said in 2001, was the one she could never quite name; the safe ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 安全（前置定语 a safe route over the hill：1989 年渔人在航海日志里记下的那件安全的路线）
B. adj. 安全／稳妥（比较级 safer than：文中两处，一处比翻山的安全路线，一处比预想）
C. adj. 安全／稳妥（最高级 the safest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 安全（表语 too safe to do：母亲觉得它太安全，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 稳妥（前置定语 a safe place for the money：叔叔把整件事称作一桩稳妥的去处）
F. adj. 稳妥（同级比较 as safe as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩放钱的稳妥去处相比）
G. adj. 稳妥（后置定语 something safe：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 稳妥（受程度副词修饰 quite safe：那位船工的评价）

items.q: a safe route over the hill
the safest route over the hill anybody
a safe place for the money
The safest place for the money in

answers.why: safe 意为“安全”，1989 年渔人在航海日志里记下的是“一件安全的路线”，此处作前置定语 a safe route over the hill。
safe 意为“安全”，此处用比较级 safer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
safe 意为“安全”，航海日志上 七月 那行字说它是渔港里最安全的一件，故用最高级 the safest route over the hill。
safe 意为“安全”，母亲认为这件东西“太安全了，谁也用不上”，too safe to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
safe 意为“稳妥”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩稳妥的去处”，此处作前置定语 a safe place for the money。
safe 意为“稳妥”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩放钱的稳妥去处一样稳妥”，同级比较用 as safe as。
safe 意为“稳妥”，航海日志上那半行字要的是“稳妥的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something safe。
safe 意为“稳妥”，邻渔港来的那位船工认为这套计划“相当稳妥”，quite 修饰原级 safe。
safe 意为“稳妥”，1999 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要稳妥”，故用比较级 safer than。
safe 意为“稳妥”，母亲 2001 年说的是“整个渔港里最稳妥的那一桩”，故用最高级 the safest place for the money。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1989 年，渔人在航海日志里记下了一件安全的路线。（a safe route over the hill）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更安全。（safer than …）
母亲觉得它太安全，谁也用不上。（too safe to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩稳妥的去处。（a safe place for the money）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩放钱的稳妥去处一样稳妥。（as safe as …）
到了 1996 年，航海日志上只剩半行字：要的是一件稳妥的东西。（something safe）
answers: In 1989 the fisherman wrote of a safe route over the hill in the logbook.
Everybody said it was safer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too safe to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a safe place for the money.
He said nobody would call it as safe as the place for the money they had once had.
By 1996 the logbook asked for nothing but something safe.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 safe 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1989 the fisherman wrote of a safe route over the hill in the logbook, and nobody forgot it.
It was the safest route over the hill in the harbour, or so the logbook says.
My mother thought it too safe to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a safe place for the money, and nobody argued with him.
The boatman from the next harbour called the plan quite safe, and everybody laughed.
The safe ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
